chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi ʿUmayr, from Jamil ibn Darrāj, from a man, from one of the two عليهما السلام:

Concerning a man who stole, or drank wine, or committed zina, and that was not known from him, and he was not apprehended until he repented and reformed, he عليه السلام said: “If he has reformed and something good is known from him, the hadd is not carried out upon him.”

Muhammad ibn Abi ʿUmayr said: I said, “Then if it was a recent matter, would it still not be carried out?” He عليه السلام said: “Even if it were five months or less, and something good has appeared from him, the hudud are not carried out upon him.”
He narrated that from some of our companions, from one of the two عليهما السلام.

key_terms.أَمْرٌ جَمِيلٌ: good and commendable conduct becoming apparent

ai.seo_question: Is the hadd punishment carried out on someone who repents and reforms before being apprehended?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a person who committed theft, drank wine, or committed zina, but was not exposed or apprehended until after sincere repentance and visible reform. It states that when upright conduct becomes evident from such a person, the hadd is not carried out upon him, even if the offense was relatively recent.
